newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may revise holding company rules - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan may revise holding company rules - report.

text.p: Japan's government is considering dropping most restrictions on the setting up of holding companies as part of efforts to deregulate the country's economy, a major financial newspaper reported on Sunday.

"Preliminary screening will not be required, nor will any reporting requirements be imposed, for holding companies with total assets of 500 billion yen ($4.27 billion) or less," the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.

"Restrictions are only likely in the case of giant holding companies with huge assets or where the company controls several major firms in more than one industrial sector. A holding company may also be banned if it has above 20 trillion yen ($170 billion) in assets," the newspaper quoted a government official as saying.

"The ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) will submit the bill, a revision of the Anti-Monopoly Law, to parliament in March, hoping to enact the revision by the beginning of 1998," the Nihon Keizai said.
Finance Ministry and LDP officials had no comment on the report.
